artists.biography:
Violent Femmes were an American alternative rock band from Milwaukee, Wisconsin, initially active between 1980 and 1987 and again from 1988 to 2009. The band performed as a trio, including: singer, guitarist and songwriter Gordon Gano, bassist Brian Ritchie, and two drummers, Victor DeLorenzo (1980-1993 and 2002-2009) and Guy Hoffman (1993-2002).

The Violent Femmes released eight studio albums and fifteen singles during the course of their career. The band found immediate success with the release of their self-titled debut album in early 1983. Featuring many of their well-known songs, including "Blister in the Sun", "Kiss Off", "Add It Up" and "Gone Daddy Gone", Violent Femmes became the band's biggest-selling album and was eventually certified platinum by the RIAA. Violent Femmes went on to become one of the most commercially successful rock bands of the 1980s and 1990s, selling over 9 million albums by 2005. After the release of their third album The Blind Leading the Naked (1986), the band's future was uncertain and they split up in 1987, when Gano and Ritchie went solo. However, they regrouped a year later, releasing the album 3 (1989). Since then, Violent Femmes' popularity continued to grow, especially in the United States where the songs "Nightmares" and "American Music" cracked the top five on the Modern Rock Tracks chart.

perplexity.description:
Hotel Last Resort is the tenth studio album by American rock band Violent Femmes, released on July 26, 2019, via Add It Up Productions and [PIAS]. Musically, the album continues the band’s signature blend of folk-punk and alternative rock, characterized by acoustic-driven melodies, sardonic lyrics, and a mix of satirical and politically charged themes. Tracks like “I Get What I Want” and “Adam Was a Man” showcase the group’s trademark quirkiness and energetic delivery, while songs such as “Hotel Last Resort” and “Not OK” delve into darker, more cynical territory. The album features guest appearances, including Tom Verlaine of Television, adding a cinematic quality to the title track.

Within the context of Violent Femmes’ discography, Hotel Last Resort arrives more than three decades after their influential 1983 debut, reaffirming their place in the American punk and folk-rock canon. While it doesn’t replicate the raw impact of their early work, the album is recognized for its deliberate songwriting and thematic depth, consolidating their legacy with a mature, reflective approach. Critical reception was mixed: some reviewers praised its vitality and satirical edge, while others found certain tracks lacking in energy or originality. Commercially, the album resonated with longtime fans but did not achieve major chart success, reflecting the band’s enduring cult status rather than mainstream breakthrough.
